title_ar: هل الصراط منصوب على متن جهنم أفقيا أم عموديا؟
title_en: Is the Bridge Set over Hell Horizontally or Vertically?
body_ar:
إن الصراط يمر فوق جهنم باعتراض فوقها فجهنم تقرب دون الجنة و يمر فوقها الناس على الصراط فمن كان من أهلها يسقط فيها بتمكن من فوقها و من كان ناجيا منها حمد الله حين رآها فإنه من تمام النعمة عليه أن يرى ما نجا منه فهذا من حكمة الله في الصراط و على رقته و حدته و ما فيه من الكلاليب و عليه ومن المراقب و الشدة ينجى الله منه ما نجا و لذلك فإن الناس يتفاوتون عليه تفاوتا عظيما فمنهم من يمر كالريح المرسلة و منهم من يمر البرق الخاطف

و منهم من يمر كأجاويد الخيل و الإبل و منهم من يمر كالرجل يشتد عدوا و منهم من يزحف على مقعدته و منهم من يزحف على بطنه فقط ثم هم في ذلك ثلاثة أقسام إما ناج مسلم لم يمسسه أي أذى و لم يلصق به شيء و إما مخدوش مرسل( خدش أي جرح)أو شق بطنه أو سقطت عينيه أو يده أو رجله بكلاليب الصراط ثم نجا بعد ذلك فإذا دخل الجنة عاد إليه ما فقد و تمت خلقته و القسم الثالث مكردس على وجهه في نار جهنم يسقط من هذه المسافة الشاهفة مسافة فوق جهنم شاهقة جدا و لذلك يكفي منها أن الأبرار الذين يمرون فوقه مبعدون عن النار لا يسمعون حسيسها مع أن حسيسها يسمع من مسيرة ألاف السنين ﴿إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولائك عنها مبعدون لا يسمعون حسيسها و هم فيما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون﴾ و مع ذلك يرونها وهنا الفرق بين الرؤية و سماع الحسيس فسماع الحسيس أبلغ تأثيرا فسماع أصواتها أبلغ تأثيرا و رعبا من مجرد الرؤية من بعد و لذلك كانت الرؤية امتنانا لأنهم يرون النار حتى يعلموا أن الله قد أنعم عليهم و نجاهم منها و لكن لا يسمعون حسيسها ليلا تتأثر قلوبهم من شدة الهول و الفزع.
body_en:
The Bridge passes above Hell, set crosswise over it. Hell is brought near, below the Garden, and people pass above it upon the Bridge. Whoever is of its people falls into it, dropping straight down from above it; and whoever is saved from it praises God when he sees it, for it belongs to the completeness of the favour shown him that he should see what he has been saved from. This is part of God's wisdom in the Bridge. For all its thinness and its sharpness, and the hooks that are on it, and the watch-posts and the severity upon it, God saves from it whoever is saved.

For that reason people vary upon it enormously. Among them is one who passes like the sent wind; among them one who passes like the flashing lightning; among them one who passes like the finest of horses and camels; among them one who passes like a man running hard; among them one who crawls on his backside; and among them one who crawls on his belly only. Then within that they fall into three classes. Either one who is saved and delivered, whom no harm at all has touched and to whom nothing has clung; or one who is scratched and let go — 'scratched', that is, wounded — or whose belly is split open, or whose eyes have fallen out, or his hand, or his foot, by the hooks of the Bridge, and who is then saved after that, so that when he enters the Garden what he lost returns to him and his form is made whole. And the third class is one flung headlong on his face into the fire of Hell, falling from this towering distance — the distance above Hell is exceedingly high.

It is enough on this head that the righteous who pass above it are kept far from the Fire and do not hear its faint sound, even though its faint sound is heard from a journey of thousands of years: {Indeed, those for whom the best has already gone forth from Us — those are kept far from it. They do not hear its faint sound, and they abide in what their souls desire} (Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ 21:101–102). And yet they do see it; and here lies the difference between seeing and hearing the faint sound. Hearing the faint sound has the more penetrating effect: hearing its sounds has a more penetrating effect, and more terror in it, than mere seeing from afar. That is why the seeing was a bestowal of favour — they see the Fire so that they may know that God has favoured them and saved them from it — but they do not hear its faint sound, lest their hearts be shaken by the intensity of the horror and the dread.

flags.arabic: هل الصراط منصوب على متن جهنم أفقيا أم عموديا؟ … يمر فوق جهنم باعتراض فوقها
flags.context: the title's question set against the answer's first clause
options: render biʿtirāḍ as 'set crosswise' and flag that neither of the title's two terms is used
render as 'horizontally', answering the title's question
render as 'transversely' and treat that as equivalent to horizontal
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The title offers the questioner's own alternatives, horizontal or vertical, and the Sheikh answers with neither word: he says the Bridge passes over Hell bi-ʿtirāḍ, athwart or across it. Rendering that as 'horizontally' would put into his mouth an answer to the question as framed, which he did not give. The English keeps his word and leaves the title's alternatives unresolved.

flags.arabic: و عليه ومن المراقب و الشدة
flags.context: the list of what is on the Bridge
options: and the watch-posts and the severity upon it
and the observation points and the hardship
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The clause و عليه ومن المراقب is ungrammatical as printed — a stray wa-ʿalayhi followed by wa-min — and al-marāqib could be marāqib ('watch-posts, look-outs') or a corruption of something else. The source is preserved in body_ar; the English gives the most plausible sense and the defect is flagged rather than smoothed away.

options: read as شاهقة ('towering') and لئلا ('lest'), as rendered here
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT — two evident transcription slips. الشاهفة is not a word and is plainly شاهقة, which the source itself uses correctly two words later ('شاهقة جدا'). ليلا is plainly لئلا. Both defective spellings are preserved in body_ar per the house rule against silently fixing the source, and the English gives the evident readings.

flags.arabic: مكردس على وجهه في نار جهنم
flags.context: the third class of those crossing the Bridge
options: flung headlong on his face into the fire of Hell
heaped up on his face in the fire of Hell
tumbled over into the fire of Hell
flags.note: mukardas is the wording of the well-known report on the crossing of the Bridge and carries the sense of being piled or flung down in a heap. The Sheikh quotes none of the report's attribution here; his whole answer is a paraphrase of it and he gives no narrator, collection or grading anywhere in the record, and none has been supplied.

Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
There is no question in the body of this record; the question is in the title alone, and the body opens directly with the answer.
The Qur'anic quotation is given in the source without a reference; the reference has been supplied per house style. The source spells أولائك for أولئك; preserved in body_ar.
'Faint sound' renders ḥasīs, the word of the verse, which the Sheikh then turns into the pivot of his closing distinction; it is kept consistent throughout so that the distinction survives.
The whole answer is a close paraphrase of the prophetic reports on the crossing, given without attribution. Nothing has been supplied.
